tutor.question: Why does a P controller leave a steady-state error, and what removes it?
tutor.answer: A Proportional (P) controller calculates its input based only on the current error, meaning it cannot completely eliminate the error for a constant reference [S1]. This happens because the controller stops adding force once the error becomes very small, leaving a "steady-state error" that remains after the system settles [S1]. The Integral (I) term removes this error by reacting to the accumulated past error; as long as any error exists, the integral keeps growing until it produces enough input to make the error zero [S1].

tutor.question: What does the second-smallest eigenvalue of the Laplacian tell us?
tutor.answer:
The second-smallest eigenvalue of the graph Laplacian is called the algebraic connectivity or Fiedler value [S2]. This value determines how fast the agents in a group agree on a common value [S1]. A larger value means the graph is better connected and the agreement happens faster [S1]. If this value is zero, the graph is not connected and the groups will never agree with each other [S2].

For example, if you have three robots trying to agree on a meeting time, a large algebraic connectivity means they will reach that time quickly because their communication links are strong [S1].
citations: Feedback Control Basics, §5 Consensus in Multi-Agent Systems

quiz.question: What condition must all poles of a continuous-time linear system satisfy for it to be stable?
quiz.feedback: Correct. The material says: 'A continuous-time linear system is stable if and only if all its poles have strictly negative real parts'. (Source: Feedback Control Basics, §3 Stability and Poles)

quiz.question: What characteristic do poles with a positive real part cause in a system's response?
quiz.feedback: Not quite: the answer is D) The response grows without bound.. The material says: 'A pole with a positive real part makes the response grow without bound: the system is unstable'. (Source: Feedback Control Basics, §3 Stability and Poles)

quiz.question: Under what condition is a continuous-time linear system classified as stable?
quiz.feedback: Correct. states that a continuous-time linear system is stable if and only if all its poles have strictly negative real parts, meaning they lie in the left half of the complex plane. (Source: Feedback Control Basics, §3 Stability and Poles)
